newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE ON COURSE TO REGAIN TOP SPOT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE ON COURSE TO REGAIN TOP SPOT.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie made the perfect start to his bid to regain command of European golf with a share of the early first round lead in the European Masters on Thursday.
He finished level with Argentine Eduardo Romero and fellow Briton Malcolm Mackenzie after a six-under-par 65 on the Alpine course.
First or second place on Sunday would lift Montgomerie above absent compatriot Ian Woosnam back into top place on the Tour money list.
At present, the Scot trails Woosnam by 68,000 pounds ($107,000). But victory in the 768,000 pounds ($1.21 million) event would boost him 60,000 pounds ($94,000) ahead.
With tournaments running out, Montgomerie would be nearly certain of finishing European number one for a fourth successive year.

Montgomerie birdied his first hole after starting at the 10th. He dropped a shot at the short 11th but was then into his stride. He birdied 13 and 15 to turn in 33 and a superb eagle three at the 536-yard first sent him to four-under.
He went five-under with a birdie at the third but dropped a shot at the following hole.
Romero, playing with Montgomerie, shot four successive birdies from the 14th to turn in 31.

With two holes to play they were both five-under but Romero went ahead with a birdie two at the eighth. Back came Montgomerie to birdie the 618 yards ninth with two massive blows, a little pitch and a four feet putt.
Mackenzie also began at the 10th and was out in a one-under 34. But he had six birdies in his second half against one bogey and ended with a flourish of three successive birdies.

Montgomerie, delighted with his form, said: "We are 5,000 feet (1,500 metres) up in the Alps here and the ball goes about 10 percent further than anywhere else we play. So you have to get your club selection just right.
"My big target this year was to win a major and I didn't do that," he said.
"So my main goal is now to win the Order of Merit again. I've been lucky enough to win it three times and I'm now in a position to win it a fourth time.

"But remember last year, after Collingtree (venue for last week's British Masters) I was lying second to Sam Torrance. This year I'm second to Ian Woosnam, so my position is the same, it's just a different player in front."
